result:
This confirms everything the exploration agent found — the code matches precisely. Here's the full trace.

## The pipeline, end to end

**1. Extracting the handle from raw text — `src/lib/mentions.ts`**

`extractMentions(body)` runs `withoutCode(body).matchAll(MENTION_PATTERN)`, where `MENTION_PATTERN = /(^|[\s(<[])@([a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,38}[a-z0-9])/gi`. `withoutCode` first strips fenced ``` ``` ``` blocks and inline `` `code` `` spans so mentions inside code aren't matched. Every captured handle is lowercased and deduped via a `Set`, returned in first-appearance order. Nothing here touches the database — it's pure string parsing.

**2. Turning the handle into a real user — `src/lib/mentions.ts` + `src/server/services/comment-service.ts`**

Taskflow has no separate username field, so `handleOf(member)` defines identity as the local part of the member's email, lowercased (`member.user.email.split("@")[0]`). `resolveMentions(body, members)` builds a `Map<handle, userId>` from a supplied member list and looks up each extracted handle in it — a comment above it states explicitly: *"Unknown handles are silently dropped — a typo must never fail the comment write."*

The member list itself comes from `resolveMentionedUsers` in `comment-service.ts`, which loads up to `MENTION_LOOKUP_LIMIT = 100` org members via `memberRepo.listMembers({ orgId, limit: 100, cursor: null })` (a single, capped page — mentioning someone past the first 100 members of a large org would silently fail to resolve), then calls `resolveMentions`. It also unions in any `clientProvided` mention IDs from the comment composer's autocomplete, but only IDs that are already in the server-resolved `known` set of real member userIds — so the server-parsed list is authoritative and untrusted client input can't inject a fake mention.

**3. What carries the list forward — `comment-service.ts::createComment`**

After permission/rate-limit checks, `createComment` calls `mentionedUserIds = await resolveMentionedUsers(...)`, persists the comment via `commentRepo.insertComment(...)` (storing `mentionedUserIds` as JSON on the row, `comment-repository.ts:~150`), and then calls `emit("comment.created", { ...actorEnvelope(actor), commentId, issueId, mentionedUserIds })`. There's no queue or background job here — `src/lib/event-bus.ts` is an in-process typed pub/sub, and `emit` awaits all subscribers via `Promise.allSettled`. The server action `src/actions/comments/create-comment.ts::createCommentAction` is the entry point that calls `createComment`; its own doc comment notes the fan-out isn't triggered inline — it happens because `NotificationService` subscribes to the event.

**4. What decides in-app / email / both / neither — `src/server/services/notification-service.ts`**

`registerFanOut()` runs once at module load and subscribes to `"comment.created"`. If `payload.mentionedUserIds.length > 0`, it calls `notify(orgId, "comment_mention", mentionedUserIds, {...})`. Inside `notify`:

- **Self-mention exclusion**: `if (recipientId === payload.actorId) continue;` — mentioning yourself never generates a row.
- **Preference lookup**: `preferenceRepo.getPreference(orgId, recipientId, "comment_mention")`; a `null` result (never touched) falls back to `DEFAULT_CHANNELS = ["in_app", "email"]`.
- **Channel resolution** (`resolveChannels`): `preference.inApp` gates the in-app channel; email requires `preference.email` **and** (`!preference.digestOnly` **or** the org's `digest_email` feature flag is enabled) — i.e., a digest-only subscriber gets email deferred to the digest job rather than sent immediately.
- **Total suppression**: `if (channels.length === 0) continue;` — a recipient who's muted everything gets no row at all, not even an unread in-app one nobody sees.

Notably there's no "already participating in thread" or "muted issue" check anywhere in this path — the only gates are self-mention and per-user/per-kind channel preferences.

**5. Writing the row and (not) sending email**

Surviving rows are batched and written by `notificationRepo.insertNotifications(orgId, rows)` (`src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts`), which is what powers the in-app bell. Critically, tagging a row with `channels: ["email"]` does **not** itself send anything — the only code path that calls `sendEmail` for mentions is `src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts::runDigestEmailJob`, run only for `digestOnly` subscribers (via `preferenceRepo.listDigestSubscribers`), bundling unread notifications through `digest-service.ts` and `email-service.ts::sendEmail` (which, per its own doc comment, just logs the draft — Taskflow has no real outbound mail transport). There's also a dedicated `src/emails/mention-email.tsx` (`MentionEmail`) template wired into `src/emails/render.ts`'s `"mention"` case, but nothing in `src/` actually calls it outside of unit tests — so a non-digest recipient's "email" channel is effectively inert in the current codebase, even though the preference/channel logic treats it as granted.
